newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Vilnius Bank to work with SocGen fund.
newsitem.headline: Vilnius Bank to work with SocGen fund.

text.p: The largest bank in Lithuania, Vilnius Bank, said it was to work with an asset management fund owned by France's Societe Generale in seeking investment opportunities.
Vilnius Bank is to work with SocGen's Emerging Europe Asset Management and find investments for its $40 million Baltic Republics Fund in Lithuania.
"We together will look for investment projects, analyse them and prepare all the information," Vilnius Bank chairman Julius Niedvaras told a news conference.
He said the bank would act as financial advisor and handle practical matters related to investing in Lithuania.
The fund owns eight percent of Vilnius Bank and usually buys 20 to 30 percent of shares of a company, investing between $1.5 million and $3.0 million, Niedvaras said.
Vilnius Bank, which has GDRs listed in Luxembourg, earlier said it made a nine-month profit of 16 million litas, up from 11.7 million litas at the half-year stage.
